bibliographic.title: Use of large language models for providing automated feedback in medical imaging education: a systematic review
bibliographic.authors: Mustafa Mohammed Al-Mashhadani, Faika Ajaz, Shaista Salman Guraya, Farah Ennab
bibliographic.citation_apa: Al-Mashhadani, M. M., Ajaz, F., Guraya, S. S., & Ennab, F. (2026). Use of large language models for providing automated feedback in medical imaging education: A systematic review. Frontiers in Medicine, 13, 1803921. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmed.2026.1803921

methodology.study_design: systematic review with descriptive synthesis and quality appraisal using ROBINS-I and GRADE
methodology.sample_description: Seven included primary studies examining automated LLM feedback for medical imaging education of radiology residents, with one study also including fellows
methodology.technology_context: LLM-generated automated feedback for trainees in medical imaging education, including fine-tuned and general-purpose LLMs

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a registered PRISMA systematic review focused on LLM automated feedback in medical imaging education within healthcare, and it explicitly emphasizes human expert oversight and hybrid human-AI feedback. However, the provided text contains no evidence of conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, audit/logging, or broader operational governance mechanisms central to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage marked central_candidate, but conversational_ai evidence is absent in the supplied text; adjudication is needed on whether human-oversight themes in non-conversational educational feedback are sufficient for central inclusion.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on front-matter text provided. Methods appear appropriate for a systematic review (PRISMA 2020, PROSPERO registration, named databases, ROBINS-I and GRADE), but full search strategy, screening procedures, and appraisal results are not visible in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The review reports a small included corpus (7 studies) and characterizes the evidence as preliminary and limited. Findings on hybrid human-AI feedback and essential human oversight are coherent in the provided text, but adequacy and relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems are limited because the focus is educational automated feedback rather than conversational AI governance.

axial_codes: LLM use in regulated healthcare education
coding.theme: Human oversight and hybrid human-AI use of LLMs in regulated medical education
coding.subtheme: Automated feedback for radiology trainees with retained expert supervision

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs may serve as supportive tools for automated feedback in medical imaging education alongside human feedback, with reported gains in accuracy, efficiency, and learner satisfaction, but current evidence remains preliminary.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes seven primary studies on LLM automated feedback for radiology trainees and highlights preference for hybrid human-AI feedback plus the essential role of human expert oversight.
synthesis.limitations: Published evidence is preliminary and limited; larger multicenter studies with standardized methods are needed before widespread adoption; current evidence supports technical feasibility more than definitive educational effectiveness.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on human oversight and hybrid human-AI deployment of LLMs in regulated healthcare education; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance, guardrails, auditability, or operational technical governance.
